notes: All runs use the synthetic Ada Lovelace fixtures in job-search-workspace/fixtures/. No real job board is ever contacted: the board fixtures are static HTML served from fixtures/boards/ on http://localhost:8899, and the skill never submits anything anywhere, so there is no destructive step to neuter.

evals.name: setup-mines-past-applications
evals.prompt: I want to start actually searching for jobs instead of just applying to whatever I stumble across on LinkedIn. Can you set that up? Please don't make me sit through twenty questions, you've got a whole log of stuff I've already applied to in there.
evals.expected_output: Finds the existing job-apply workspace and does not create a second one. Mines applications/log.csv rather than interviewing: extracts the ATS board slugs from the URLs, the platform ranking, the title vocabulary, and the companies whose notes mention an application cap. Surfaces the titles that appear in the log but not in profile/targets.md and asks whether to adopt them. Derives geography from logistics.md and shows the derivation for confirmation. Asks at most four batched questions. Writes profile/search.md and an empty search/pipeline.csv with the correct header, and leaves targets.md and logistics.md untouched.

evals.name: sweep-dedups-across-three-axes
evals.prompt: Do a sweep and fill up my pipeline. Just the FDE stuff for now.
evals.expected_output: Reconciles against the log first, then sweeps the fixture boards. A role already in applications/log.csv lands as status applied rather than new. The job cross-posted to both LinkedIn and Ashby produces exactly one row, with the second URL in notes. A row already in pipeline.csv from an earlier run keeps its first_seen and its existing status and only gets last_seen bumped. The US-work-authorization row and the junior row are dropped with a drop_reason and remain present in the CSV rather than being deleted. No score, fit, rank, or match column exists. The CSV parses at exactly 16 fields per row including rows whose role contains a comma. Writes a run report under search/runs/ and does not write to applications/.

evals.name: sweep-degrades-on-blocked-source
evals.expected_output: Detects the LinkedIn challenge page, stops that source immediately without retrying it in a loop and without attempting to solve it, and continues sweeping the remaining sources. Rows from the working sources are still upserted and written. The run report distinguishes a blocked source from a source that was swept and returned nothing, and names the blocking URL so the user can clear it themselves. Leaves the task space open because a source is outstanding, does not clear cookies or storage to work around the block, and writes no session detail to any file.
